facts.fact: Decree no. 2015-79 of 4 February 2015, signed by the President, sets the filing, authorisation, withdrawal and fine-recovery procedures under law no. 2013-450 of 19 June 2013 on personal data protection.

The decree names ARTCI as the body that receives declarations, rules on authorisation requests within one month, and imposes withdrawals and fines under the 2013 law; it shows no appointment of members or acting decisions.

The decree, made under law no. 2013-450 of 19 June 2013 on personal data protection, treats the law as operating, with filing fees, prior authorisations and fines up to FCFA 500 million on repeat breach.

facts.fact: ARTCI, described as the Autorite de Protection, said it initiated a national study of controllers' compliance with Law no. 2013-450.
ARTCI refers to compliance with the requirements in force under Law no. 2013-450 of 19 June 2013 on personal data protection.
ARTCI mandated OKTO Technologies to collect data from public and private entities from 26 January to 25 May 2026 for a national census and compliance evaluation under the law.

Agence Ecofin reports that the 2013 personal data protection law requires organisations processing data in Cote d'Ivoire to declare to ARTCI or obtain prior authorisation, with fines up to 10 million FCFA.

facts.fact: ARTCI is reported as acting as the regulator, having received 210 complaints and made 18 inspections and keeping the national file of data protection correspondents.
An order of August 2024 set the profile and conditions of employment of data protection correspondents, whose designation exempts organisations from some declaration formalities.
ARTCI had imposed no financial penalty despite 210 complaints and 18 inspections, ten years after the law.
On 2 July 2026 ARTCI launched Certinum, a platform for online authorisation requests, compliance certificates and video surveillance filings, first tried by ONECI and the Treasury.
